That slide tracks the tape: QQQ fell ~12% and IWM ~2.6% over the same span (Yahoo bars). There is no usable option chain (ATM not two-sided, OI 269), so no implied move. My own reconstruction of the last seven report days at about 13:00 ET: Feb-25 -2%, May-25 about +1 to +3%, Aug-25 about +1%, Nov-25 about +2%, Feb-26 +20%, May-26 +14.5%, Aug-26 +2.4%. The last three each gapped up 8-13% at the open and partly faded. Consensus: Q3 revenue $57.5M (Benzinga) to $58.6M (Chartmill), EPS $0.02-0.05, Q4 revenue $62.4M (Benzinga). The ages of those estimates are unavailable. Guide (2026-08-12): Q3 revenue $55-60M, adj EBITDA margin 0-3%, and H2 revenue about 15% above H1. On H1 = $103.8M that gives H2 about $119.4M and an implied Q4 of about $61.9M at the Q3 midpoint, so Q4 consensus already sits a touch above the guide's implied Q4. Track record: revenue at the top end or above the guide in each of the last four quarters (Q2 $55.3M vs $51-55M). Positioning: short interest 0.74M shares on 2026-10-30, about 1.7% of 42.97M shares, 2.4 days to cover. Artisan fell to 4.1% (13G/A 2026-11-12). Cash and investments of about $451M are 63% of the ~$713M market cap, and about $60M of buyback authorization remains.
view: This looks like a beat-and-raise-type print in a weak tape. The released number will probably be a beat. Kornit has landed at or above the top of its range four quarters running, and the Q3 range ($55-60M) is wide with consensus at or just above the midpoint. Services and AIC (ARR +79% y/y in Q2) make about 80% of revenue recurring. The adj EBITDA margin should also look fine. The shekel has weakened from ~2.82 per dollar in May to ~3.0-3.1 through Q3 and 3.25 now (+8% since the August guide), which cuts the Israel-based cost base, though hedges blunt it. The line the stock trades on is the forward view, not Q3: the Q4 guide against the $62.4M consensus, plus ARR and the margin path. That is genuinely two-sided. If Q3 lands near $60M because Atlas MATRIX upgrades for the strategic customer came in Q3 rather than early Q4, as management said they would, then keeping H2 at +15% implies Q4 at only ~$59.4M, below consensus. A raised H2 view, like the Q3 raise last time, would instead extend the run of positive reactions. Positioning slightly favours upside: shorts are light, the stock has given back the post-Q2 level in a tech sell-off rather than on company news, and cash floors the downside. Reaction history is skewed positive at the open, but recent gaps faded, and a 13:00 exit on a weak-tape day takes some of the fade. I could not find dated, independent evidence since the August call that the consensus has not already absorbed. The one lead (Amazon's 1 June 2026 Merch royalty cut, which could lower strategic-customer ink volume) predates the August H2 outlook and has no volume data behind it. Net: a mild upward tilt, no edge I would bet on.
unpriced: Possibly the Q4 EBITDA-margin guide, helped by an ~8% weaker shekel since the August guide. That move appeared after the last estimates were set and is not shown in any preview I found. It is small and partly hedged, and it lands on a line (margin) that moves this stock less than revenue and ARR do.

recommendation.reason: The beat is likely, but a consistent beater's beat is mostly in the bar already (consensus at or above the guide midpoint, Q4 consensus above the implied H2 split). The deciding line, the Q4 guide, turns on the timing of MATRIX upgrades and peak-season orders, and I found no dated public evidence on either. Light shorts, a market-driven pullback and a cash floor tilt it slightly up, but nowhere near 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide whose midpoint is at or above ~$64M (H2 raised) would make up likely; a Q4 midpoint below ~$60M (Q3 strength explained as upgrade timing) would make down likely.

self_critique: For the downside: the stock has gapped up and faded on each of the last three prints. Tech is in a sharp drawdown, so a bmo beat may be sold into by 13:00. Q4 consensus already exceeds the implied guide. Management dodged the question on strategic-customer demand after Amazon's royalty change. A Q4 guide of, say, $58-63M would read as a cut and could take the stock down 8-10%. For the upside: four straight top-end beats, a market-driven pullback, light shorts and 63% of the market cap in cash could produce another +10-20% day like February or May. Both tails are fat, which is why I stay near 50.
